substance_use.none_key: ITEM None of the above substances Score

templates.75: I used more of a substance (e.g., {endorsed_substances}) than I had planned to, or for longer than I had planned to.
templates.76: I kept using a substance (e.g., {endorsed_substances}) even though it caused or worsened a problem with my mental or physical health.
templates.77: I spent a lot of time acquiring, using, or recovering from the effects of a substance (e.g., {endorsed_substances}).
templates.78: I needed more of a substance (e.g., {endorsed_substances}) to get the effect I wanted, or experienced less effect from the same amount.
templates.79: I had a strong desire or urge to use a substance (e.g., {endorsed_substances}).
templates.80: I kept using a substance (e.g., {endorsed_substances}) even though it caused or worsened problems in my relationships.
templates.81: I wanted to cut down on my use of a substance (e.g., {endorsed_substances}), or tried to and couldn't.
templates.82: I used a substance (e.g., {endorsed_substances}) to relieve or avoid withdrawal symptoms due to stopping use of that substance.

descriptions.spectrum:Detachment: Measures disengagement from social and emotional life, together with low mood: reduced interest and pleasure, hopelessness and diminished self-worth, withdrawal from relationships and social contact, and a muted or unexpressed emotional range. In this measure, the dimension also encompasses reduced interest in sexual and romantic relationships.
descriptions.spectrum:Eating Pathology: Assesses disturbances of eating and body image, including fear of weight gain, the influence of weight or shape on self-evaluation, restrictive eating, and distress associated with overeating.
descriptions.spectrum:Externalising: Measures behaviour and emotion directed outward against other people, rules, or norms — a broad spectrum spanning impulsive, reckless, or aggressive conduct, manipulation and self-interest, reduced concern for others, and outwardly directed anger.
descriptions.spectrum:Harmful Substance Use: Assesses the core features of problematic alcohol and other drug use, including craving, loss of control over use, tolerance and withdrawal, continued use despite harm, and use in dangerous situations.
descriptions.spectrum:Internalising: Represents the broad propensity to experience negative emotions turned inward. This wide-ranging spectrum spans low mood, worry and anxious arousal, fear-based avoidance, social withdrawal, and trauma-related distress with disturbed sleep.
descriptions.spectrum:Mania: Measures the dimension of elevated and expansive mood. In this measure, it is assessed through euphoric mood, heightened sociability and talkativeness, unrestrained emotional expression, and enjoyment of attention.
descriptions.spectrum:Neurodevelopmental and Cognitiv: Encompasses difficulties of neurodevelopment and cognition — a broad spectrum spanning social communication, attentional and sensory regulation, ritualised and inflexible behaviour, and problems with memory, attention, and everyday cognitive functioning.
descriptions.spectrum:Somatoform: Assesses the experience of physical symptoms and bodily concern — pain, palpitations and breathlessness, temperature sensations, unsteadiness and slowed thinking or movement — together with health anxiety and disturbances of sleep and eating.
descriptions.spectrum:Thought Disorder: Measures disruptions to the ordinary integration of perception, thought, and consciousness, spanning psychotic-like experiences and beliefs, dissociative experiences, and associated physical and behavioural changes.
descriptions.subspectrum:Cognitive Difficulties: Assesses problems with everyday cognitive functioning: attention and concentration, memory, word-finding, planning and decision-making, mental speed, and the capacity to manage everyday tasks, possessions, and living spaces.
descriptions.subspectrum:Neurodevelopmental: Captures traits and difficulties commonly associated with neurodevelopmental conditions: social communication difficulties, overactivity and pressured speech, sensory sensitivity, unusually intense interests, and ritualised or inflexible behaviour.
descriptions.subfactor:Antagonism: Measures self-interested and manipulative interpersonal behaviour, including deceit, entitlement, attention-seeking, and deliberately annoying others.
descriptions.subfactor:Antisocial Behaviour: Represents the dimension of aggressive and harmful conduct. In this measure, it is assessed through physical aggression towards people, animals, or property.
descriptions.subfactor:Callousness: Assesses reduced empathy and emotional responsiveness to others: indifference to others' feelings, lack of concern about causing hurt, and a sense of personal superiority or entitlement.
descriptions.subfactor:Disinhibition: Measures deficient restraint over behaviour: acting without regard for consequences, recklessness, carelessness, and feeling or acting out of control.
descriptions.subfactor:Externalised Negative Affect: Captures negative emotion directed outward at other people and circumstances: irritability, anger and verbal outbursts, resentment, mistrust of others, and blaming others for one's own difficulties.
descriptions.subfactor:Distress: Represents the core negative-affect dimension of internalising — a broad blend of low mood and diminished pleasure, worry and anxious arousal, emotional lability, guilt and negative self-evaluation, and suicidality.
descriptions.subfactor:Dysregulated Sleep and Trauma: Assesses post-traumatic distress together with disturbed sleep: distress and avoidance connected to a traumatic experience, and difficulty falling or staying asleep.
descriptions.subfactor:Fear: Measures the phobic aspects of anxiety: fear and avoidance cued by particular objects, situations, or concerns — public or enclosed spaces, social scrutiny, specific phobic stimuli, illness and dying, bodily appearance, and rejection or abandonment.
descriptions.subfactor:Social Withdrawal: Assesses behavioural disengagement from social life — avoidance of and discomfort in social situations, anxiety about public spaces or being away from home, and diminished interest in other people — alongside lowered mood and enjoyment.
descriptions.subfactor:Difficulties with Organisation: Assesses difficulty keeping one's possessions and living environment manageable: losing needed items, clutter that limits the use of living areas, difficulty discarding possessions, and needing help with everyday household tasks.
descriptions.subfactor:Forgetfulness: Measures changes in memory and familiar abilities: difficulty recalling recent events, declining ease with familiar skills, and trouble finding one's way in familiar places.
descriptions.subfactor:Neurocognitive Impairment: Assesses a broad range of cognitive difficulties spanning attention, concentration, multitasking, memory, word-finding, mental speed and effort, planning and decision-making, and independence in daily activities.
descriptions.subfactor:Altered Sensation and Attentio: Measures dysregulation of attention, activity, speech, and sensory experience: restlessness and overactivity, pressured or excessive speech, sensitivity to sensory input, and unusually intense interests.
descriptions.subfactor:Ritualised Behaviour: Assesses rigid and repetitive patterns of behaviour: insistence on sameness, perfectionism, and repetitive acts performed to manage intrusive thoughts or distress, or to prevent something bad from happening.
descriptions.subfactor:Social Communication Difficult: Measures difficulty understanding and using communication in social interaction: following what others mean, holding reciprocal conversations, responding when others make contact, reading and using non-verbal cues, and adapting behaviour to the social context.
descriptions.subfactor:Dysregulated Eating: Represents the dimension of disrupted eating patterns that present alongside other physical symptoms. In this measure, it is assessed through eating large amounts of food in the absence of hunger.
descriptions.subfactor:Dysregulated Sleep: Assesses disturbance of the sleep–wake cycle as a physical presentation: difficulty falling or staying asleep, and excessive daytime sleepiness despite adequate sleep.
descriptions.subfactor:Somatic Symptoms: Measures the experience of distressing bodily symptoms — pain and muscle tension, palpitations and breathlessness, temperature sensations, unsteadiness and slowed thinking or movement — together with anxiety about one's physical health.
descriptions.subfactor:Dissociative Experiences: Assesses disruptions to the ordinary integration of consciousness, perception, memory, and identity: detachment from oneself or one's surroundings, gaps in memory, experiences of separate self-states, and sudden losses of control over thought, emotion, or behaviour.
descriptions.subfactor:Positive Psychosis: Measures psychotic-like experiences and beliefs: perceptions that others do not share, beliefs held despite contrary evidence, experiences of thought interference, and thinking or behaviour that others find strange.
descriptions.subfactor:Uncontrollable Physical Sympto: Assesses involuntary movements and unusual bodily sensations: trembling, chills, numbness or tingling, unsteadiness, and a sense of being slowed. In this measure, the dimension also encompasses being seen by others as odd or unusual.
